sentences.text: 3 : M s . K h u s h b o o D u a , A d v o c a t e ________________________________________________________ Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput, Order on Board 16.10.2023

1 ) This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "the act of 1988") by the appellants/claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of the First Additional Presiding Officer, Raipur (CG) in Claim Case No.255/2015 awarding a compensation of Rs.8,86,800/- in their favour.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of the First Additional Presiding Officer, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Neutral Citation 2) In a claim application filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, by the appellants/claimants, the learned tribunal has awarded Rs.8,86,800/- as compensation on account of death of the deceased namely Prakash Chandra Yadu in an accident that occurred on 14.02.2015.

Smt. Janki Yadu vs Mubarak Ansari on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167624259/
1
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1/driver of the offending vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration No. OD-18-A-7511.
The offending vehicle was owned by respondent No.2/owner and insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.

The deceased was aged about 27 years and was working in Bore-well machine as Banking & recovery and used to earn Rs.10,500/- per month as per (Ex.P- 9), and thus, total amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.8,86,800/- was claimed under various heads.
The claim was resisted by driver, owner and insurance company of the offending vehicle on various grounds.
3) The learned tribunal framed as many as 6 issues and all the issues have been decided in favour of claimants and against the insurance company and awarded amount of compensation as stated above.

4) Ms. Prachi Singh, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the deceased was earning Rs.10,500/- per month and his income was also proved by calling the witness Sandeep (PW-3) and exhibited his salary certificate (Ex.P-9) and his attendance register (Ex.P-8).

Therefore,
the assessment of the compensation ought to have done on the basis of the salary certificate.
Apart from this, she submits that the compensation under the head of filial consortium has not been awarded, therefore, the compensation may be suitably enhanced.
Neutral Citation 5)
Mr. A. D. Kuldeep, learned counsel for respondents No.1 & 2/driver/owner submits that the liability to pay the compensation is upon the insurance company.

6) Ms. Khushboo Dua, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company vehemently supported the award and submitted that the learned tribunal after due appreciation of evidence of Sandeep (PW-3) and all relevant factors, came to a specific finding disbelieving the Ex.P-8 and Ex.P-9.
She further reading over the statement of PW-3 submits that it appears that exhibits were framed in order to obtain the compensation.

There is anomaly in the statement as well as in the documents and the learned tribunal has rightly disbelieved, therefore, the appeal has no merit and is liable to be dismissed.
7) Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their submissions and perused the record.
8) On examination of the record, the finding with regard to income of the deceased appears to be a reasonable and based on proper appreciation of evidence.

The learned tribunal has minutely scrutinize the statement of witnesses, particularly, PW-3 and gave a categorical finding that the appellants/claimants could not prove the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.10,500/-.
In the opinion of this Court there is no illegality in recording such finding, therefore, it is affirmed.

The tribunal has considered the monthly income of deceased to Rs.6,000/- and the annual being Rs.72,000/- and added 40% towards future prospect; deducted  for personal expenses and applied multiplier of 17; Rs.8,56,800/- towards loss of dependency; Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs. 15,000/- towards loss of estate.

In view of Neutral Citation judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi and others reported in Smt. Janki Yadu vs Mubarak Ansari on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167624259/
2 (2017) 16 SCC 680 there appears to be no error committed by learned tribunal in assessing the compensation, however, in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors; (2018) 18 SCC 130, the appellants/claimants are entitled to Rs.80,000/- (40,000/-each) towards filial consortium.
